problem: Original parallel Depth still passes150/150 at u180, then loses26 cases in S01/D03 byu184. Full-return tails recover the later control losses but introduce other losses and fail their all-check gate. Component swaps and entropy removal also failed. Cross-scene regression is observed; gradient interference is not yet established.
hypotheses: Repeated scene-specific conflict makes the shared Actor update locally worsen a previously mastered scene.
Scene gradients are themselves noisy across world groups or conditional action draws, so one negative inter-scene cosine is not evidence of stable task interference.
scope: Measurement only; no optimizer continuation or evaluation replay. Scenes are the existing training strata, not new tasks or Actor inputs. Full-batch Adam probes are local counterfactuals, not the native16-minibatch update.

sampling.shared_initial_state: Both copies retain complete u180 physical state, episode clocks, recurrent memory, optimizer and objective history. No evaluation seeds/data enter the objective.
sampling.groups: Eight existing contiguous training scenes, each split into its first/last4worlds; all16half-group losses use the original global advantage normalization.

measurements: Per-scene and half-scene PPO Actor gradients, including original0.005entropy and trainablelog_std
Inter-scene, within-scene half-group and cross-replicate cosine similarities; retain norms and Actor-only versus full-variable results
Predicted directional change and actual same-batch surrogate loss after one full-batch Adam step from original moments
Average of16half-gradients must match independently differentiated full-batch loss; source learner counters/state stay unchanged
selection_gate: Only consider a separate PCGrad continuation if a pair involving S01 or D03 has cosine<-0.1 in BOTH draws, BOTH pair members have positive half-group cosine in each draw and cross-draw scene cosine>0.5, AND S01 or D03 has normalized gradient dot Adam delta>0.1 in both draws with actual surrogate loss increasing. Thresholds are preregistered project diagnostic choices, not a published convergence guarantee. Also require the critical scene gradient to have normalized dot product>0.1 with the NEGATIVE aggregate gradient in both draws, so harm is not attributed only to inherited Adam momentum.
falsifier: Failure of the combined gate does not establish scene-gradient projection as the next intervention. In particular, unstable within-scene directions indicate sampling variability rather than reproducible scene identity alone. No automatic PCGrad integration from negative cosine counts.
limitations: Two conditional draws do not estimate population gradients or establish a unique root cause. Local surrogate harm is not episode-level capability loss; no curvature theorem or stability acceptance is inferred.

references.claim: Negative gradient cosine defines conflict, but conflict alone is not necessarily harmful; magnitude and curvature matter. PCGrad is a real published intervention, not presumed necessary here.
Official policy-optimization batch-size research motivates distinguishing sampling noise from task-specific interference; no new algorithm is adopted in this probe.
